automation.name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.policy: Include only public items visibly published or updated within the last 2 days relative to run time. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, boundary-only, stale, duplicate, or non-security dates.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

federation_context.local_scope: Security-specific AI threats, model and prompt security, agent/tool security, data/privacy, identity/access, supply-chain, assurance, governance, and incident response.
federation_context.routing_rule: Broad companies, products, models, frameworks, MCP servers, and general development practices route upstream; this artifact keeps security-specific boundaries, affected versions, mitigations, confidence notes, and ingest follow-ups.

findings.title: AiSOC response actions and realtime service vulnerability cluster
findings.summary: Five AiSOC CVEs disclose missing authentication or authorization on response-action and realtime APIs, hard-coded JWT verification defaults, tenant portfolio authorization bypass, and CrowdStrike RTR command injection in versions before 12.0.0.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AiSOC versions 5.1.0, 7.2.0, 7.5.0, and 9.0.0 before 12.0.0 depending on endpoint; command-injection and control-plane endpoints are the security boundary.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AiSOC is positioned as an AI SOC/response-action surface; unauthenticated event injection and response-action command execution can turn an AI-assisted security operations control plane into a tenant crossover, false-event, or command-execution path.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep the endpoint, auth, tenant, JWT, and command-execution security implications locally. Route any broad AiSOC product overview upstream only if needed later.

findings.confidence: High for public CVE timing and high-level impact; fixed-version and vendor remediation wording should be rechecked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify whether 12.0.0 is the unified fixed release for every AiSOC CVE in the cluster.
Check whether any vendor advisory or release note adds deployment-specific mitigations beyond the CVE text.

findings.title: Claude Code organization policy check used stored API key before valid team sign-in
findings.summary: Claude Code selected a locally stored API key ahead of the user's valid Claude Enterprise or Team sign-in while fetching organization policy, creating a credential-precedence boundary issue.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Claude Code policy-fetch authentication path; exact affected and fixed versions require vendor confirmation.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding-agent policy enforcement depends on the correct organization identity and credential source. Key precedence mistakes can undermine enterprise policy, audit, or least-privilege controls.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep local credential-precedence and enterprise-policy control implications. Broad Claude Code product context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence: Medium-high for CVE existence and boundary; affected version and remediation detail need primary vendor recheck.
follow_up_actions: Find the vendor advisory or release note before durable synthesis.
Check whether existing Claude Code credential-governance leaves already cover this boundary.

findings.title: JetBrains Rider AI Assistant third-party skill auto-update without confirmation
findings.summary: JetBrains Rider before 2026.2.1 could allow AI Assistant to auto-update third-party skills without user confirmation.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: JetBrains Rider before 2026.2.1; AI Assistant third-party skill update boundary.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent or assistant skills are executable or behavior-shaping supply-chain inputs. Silent updates weaken approval, provenance, and change-control gates for AI-assisted development environments.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep the skill-update security control locally. General AI-assisted development workflow implications route to ai-dev-wiki if they become durable practice guidance.

findings.confidence: Medium; CVE text is concise and needs vendor advisory confirmation during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Locate JetBrains advisory text for severity, exploitability, and fixed build evidence.
Compare with existing skill/plugin supply-chain pages before creating a new leaf.

findings.title: Moodle AI editor image-generation capability check bypass
findings.summary: Moodle's AI editor placement image-generation web service used an incorrect capability check, allowing authenticated users to invoke image generation without holding the required capability.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Moodle AI editor placement image-generation web service; exact Moodle versions require advisory reconciliation.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI feature invocation must obey role and capability checks, especially where generation features can incur cost, process sensitive context, or produce moderated content.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep local least-privilege and AI feature authorization implications. Broad Moodle product context is upstream or out of scope.

findings.confidence: Medium-high for CVE timing and authorization boundary; version/fix details need vendor confirmation.
follow_up_actions: Locate Moodle security announcement for affected versions and patch releases.
Check whether the local identity-and-access folder already has an AI-feature authorization leaf pattern to extend.

findings.title: Laravel AI SDK SSRF via client-supplied file URLs
findings.summary: The Laravel AI SDK advisory GHSA-6qhr-3g93-pxhw reports SSRF in laravel/ai 1.0.0: the Vercel AI SDK and AG-UI adapters accepted URL file parts and fetched them server-side without destination validation. Version 1.0.1 adds URL, private-address, redirect-hop, and DNS-rebinding guards.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: laravel/ai >= 1.0.0 and < 1.0.1; applications exposing Vercel or AG-UI adapters to untrusted clients.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Chat file-part ingestion can turn model attachment handling into network access to metadata services, localhost, or private networks, and the fetched response can be surfaced to the model output.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep the SSRF and chat-file ingestion boundary locally. General Laravel AI SDK development usage belongs in ai-dev-wiki only if a broader practice page is needed.

findings.confidence: High; primary GitHub advisory provided affected and patched versions, CVSS, CWE, and workaround.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare with existing agent/tool SSRF leaves and avoid duplicating a generic SSRF pattern page.
Check whether Laravel MCP open-redirect advisory is stale for this run and only mention as exclusion unless a fresh update appears.

findings.title: MCP Python SDK OAuth metadata trust flaw

visible_dates.source: CSA citation to GitHub Security Advisory

findings.summary: Public reports on GHSA-qx49-fqc8-xw99 describe a flaw in the official MCP Python SDK where malicious MCP servers could redirect OAuth token exchange and receive client secrets, authorization codes, and PKCE proof keys. CSA reports affected ranges 1.9.1 through 1.29.1 and 2.0.0 through 2.1.1, fixed in 1.30.0 and 2.2.0.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MCP Python SDK 1.9.1-1.29.1 and 2.0.0-2.1.1 for HTTP OAuth client flows; fixed in 1.30.0 and 2.2.0 per CSA report.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP clients commonly connect agents to third-party tools and identity providers. Treating server-supplied OAuth metadata as trusted can leak non-human or delegated credentials to attacker-controlled token endpoints.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep identity, credential, and MCP trust-boundary implications locally. Broad MCP protocol and SDK background belongs upstream.

findings.confidence: Medium-high. Multiple public reports provide consistent affected/fixed ranges, but the primary GitHub advisory did not render cleanly through the available fetch path and should be rechecked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Re-fetch the GitHub Security Advisory directly during ingest if possible.
Check whether existing MCP authorization-model or identity-sprawl leaves should link to this as concrete evidence.

findings.title: Obot composite MCP route authorization bypass
findings.summary: Obot 0.21.1 through 0.24.1 contains an authorization bypass where the checkUI deny list omits the /mcp-connect-composite/ route, allowing basic-role users with server IDs to connect to MCP servers otherwise blocked by UI/API policy.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP server access is delegated tool authority. A route-specific ACL omission can let lower-privilege users reach restricted tools through an alternate connection path.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep route-level authorization bypass locally. Broad Obot product context, if needed, belongs upstream.

findings.confidence: High for CVE timing and route-level boundary; fixed-version confirmation needs vendor/reference check.
follow_up_actions: Deduplicate against existing Obot MCP connect and registry authorization pages during ingest.
Check whether this is a material delta from CVE-2026-101084 or belongs as an update to the same local leaf.

findings.title: Budibase AI table generation SSRF
findings.summary: Budibase through 3.41.0 contains SSRF in AI table generation because uploadUrl uses raw node-fetch rather than Budibase's guarded fetch path.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Budibase through 3.41.0; AI table generation uploadUrl network-fetch path.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI data-table generation workflows can cross from user input into server-side network retrieval. Missing SSRF guards can expose internal services or metadata endpoints through AI-assisted import flows.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep AI-generation SSRF boundary locally. Broad Budibase low-code platform context is upstream or out of scope.

findings.confidence: High for CVE text; fixed version and patch mechanism need vendor reference before durable synthesis.
follow_up_actions: Locate Budibase patch or advisory to confirm fixed version.
Compare with Laravel AI SDK SSRF finding for possible shared AI-file/network-ingestion pattern.

findings.title: ByteCoreStack MCP Connector privilege-escalation cluster
findings.summary: Two ByteCoreStack MCP Connector for AI Tools records describe privilege escalation affecting versions up to 1.2.3 and up to 1.2.2, including an execute_tool/wp_update_user_meta path that can grant elevated privileges.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ByteCoreStack MCP Connector for AI Tools <= 1.2.3 for CVE-2026-19807 and <= 1.2.2 for CVE-2026-103068.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP connectors embedded in WordPress can expose administrative mutation tools through AI-tool execution paths. Privilege escalation in those tools undermines least-privilege control for delegated site actions.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep MCP connector privilege-escalation boundary locally. Exclude generic WordPress-plugin context unless the MCP tool path is central.

findings.confidence: Medium-high; CVE text is concrete but affected-version overlap and whether both records are distinct need ingest reconciliation.
follow_up_actions: Reconcile whether the two CVEs describe distinct vulnerable paths or overlapping records for the same plugin issue.
Look for Wordfence, Patchstack, or vendor advisory details before durable synthesis.

findings.title: Office-PowerPoint-MCP-Server path traversal
findings.summary: Office-PowerPoint-MCP-Server through 2.0.7 allows MCP callers to read and write files outside the working directory by supplying absolute paths or ../ sequences.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Office-PowerPoint-MCP-Server through 2.0.7; MCP file read/write path boundary.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Document automation MCP servers often run with access to user workspaces. Path traversal lets delegated tool calls escape the intended working directory and touch unrelated files.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep local path traversal and delegated file-authority implications. Broad MCP server catalog context belongs upstream.

findings.confidence: Medium-high for CVE timing and vulnerability class; fixed version and primary repository references need follow-up.
follow_up_actions: Locate upstream repository/advisory to confirm remediation and whether a patched version exists.
Compare with existing MCP filesystem path-boundary leaves before adding a new page.

findings.title: Joyland AI mobile app credential, TLS, WebView, and cleartext-traffic cluster
findings.summary: Six Joyland AI app CVEs disclose hard-coded GeTui push-service credentials, JavaScript injection into WebView content, accepted arbitrary TLS certificates, missing hostname verification, permitted cleartext HTTP traffic, and invalid SSL certificate acceptance in an advertisement WebView.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Joyland AI mobile app; exact app versions require source-advisory reconciliation.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI companion/chat applications process conversational content and notification channels. Mobile credential, TLS, and WebView flaws create privacy, spoofing, interception, and arbitrary-content injection risks around AI user sessions.

upstream_routing.notes: Keep user-data, credential, TLS, and mobile AI-app security implications locally. Broad app/provider context routes upstream if needed.

findings.confidence: Medium. CVE records are direct and in-window, but vendor remediation and affected app versions need follow-up.
follow_up_actions: Find primary research/vendor disclosure for exact affected versions and remediation status.
Decide during ingest whether to create one mobile AI app cluster leaf or split credential/TLS/WebView boundaries.
